meta.title: Operation of Serological Water Bath in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To provide controlled temperature water bath conditions for incubating phytochemical reactions, warming extraction solvents, and performing colour development reactions in crude drug analysis.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for temperature-controlled incubations in qualitative phytochemical tests, Fehling's test, Millon's test, and Biuret reactions.
procedure: Fill the serological water bath tank with distilled water to the recommended fill level.
Switch on the unit and set the required temperature using the thermostat: typically 37°C for enzyme reactions; 60–80°C for heating extracts; 100°C for boiling water bath.
Allow the bath to reach and stabilize at the set temperature — verify with a calibrated thermometer placed inside the water.
Place test tubes, flasks, or bottles containing the reaction mixture into the bath rack or tube holders.
Ensure the sample level in the tubes is below the water level in the bath for effective heat transfer.
Begin timing the incubation once the bath has reached the set temperature and samples are inserted.
Monitor the temperature periodically — note any drift and correct using the thermostat.
After the incubation period, remove samples using tongs or heatproof gloves.
Immediately proceed to the next step of the phytochemical test (e.g., colour observation).
After use, switch off the water bath.
If the bath is to be stored, drain the water, clean the tank with dilute disinfectant, and dry thoroughly.
Refill with fresh distilled water before the next use.
Log temperature, duration, samples processed, and operator name in the equipment register.
precautions: Never allow the water level to drop below the minimum fill line — dry heating damages the heating element.
Do not use tap water — mineral deposits foul the heating element; always use distilled water.
Use stainless steel or glass vessels — plastic containers may deform at high temperatures.
Do not heat sealed, air-tight containers — pressure build-up can cause explosive venting.
Use tongs or heatproof gloves when removing samples from hot water baths.
Regularly check the temperature with a calibrated thermometer — thermostat calibration drifts over time.
Drain and clean the bath weekly when in continuous use — algae and mineral deposits accumulate.
Do not leave the water bath switched on unattended at temperatures above 80°C.
